cards.explanation: The answer is Jerusalem, friends. He says she's "…as beautiful, my darling, as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem…" (Song of Solomon 6:4). Two cities in one breath, and I think he's just warming up. If I tried that with my cookies, I'd run out of cities and start comparing them to my apron.

The word is overcome, friends. He says, "Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me." (Song of Solomon 6:5). Her eyes win, and he's the one waving the white flag. I think a man who compares her to an army with banners knows exactly how a battle like this ends.

The picture is hair flowing down, friends. He says her hair is "…like a flock of goats streaming down from Gilead." (Song of Solomon 6:5). Streaming down is the whole picture: long, flowing hair coming down like a herd on a hillside. Only this man could say that and mean it as the nicest thing in the world.

The answer is True, friends. He says, "each has its twin, and not one of them is lost." (Song of Solomon 6:6). Every tooth has its partner, and none are missing. It's like a cookie box where every cutter shape comes in a pair and not one is missing from the box.

The word is unique, friends. Sixty queens, eighty concubines and maidens without number, "…but my dove, my perfect one, is unique…" (Song of Solomon 6:8-9). He counts up the whole crowd and then says there's still only one like her. In my bakery that's like a cookie nobody else can copy.

The answer is True, friends. He calls his dove "…the favorite of the mother who bore her." (Song of Solomon 6:9). So the one who knew her from the very beginning loves her best. I think that's a pretty good review to get from your own mom.

They call her blessed, friends. The text says, "The maidens see her and call her blessed…" (Song of Solomon 6:9). They see her, and they call her blessed. That's a good word to get from a crowd, and mine usually just takes the cookies and runs.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, "the queens and concubines sing her praises." (Song of Solomon 6:9). So it isn't only the maidens who speak well of her. The queens and concubines do it too, and I think that's a lot of praise for one dove.

She shines like lights in the sky, friends. The question says she shines "…like the dawn, as fair as the moon, as bright as the sun, as majestic as the stars in procession?" (Song of Solomon 6:10). Dawn, moon, sun and stars are all lights in the sky. That's a lot of sky for one person to carry.

The word is budding, friends. The speaker went down "…to see if the vines were budding or the pomegranates were in bloom." (Song of Solomon 6:11). So the grove trip is about checking for new growth. It's like peeking in the oven to see if the dough is rising.

The answer is False, friends. The speaker says, "Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the royal chariots of my people." (Song of Solomon 6:12). The speaker didn't realize it before it happened. So knowing all along isn't what the verse says.
